points.description: Asynchronous transmission: each character is sent as a self-contained unit framed by a start bit and a stop bit; simple/cheap but gives low transmission rate.
points.partial_credit: Half if only start/stop bits per character are given, or only simple/low-rate stated, without the other.

points.description: Synchronous transmission: many characters are grouped into a continuous stream/frames (delimited by SYN or flag); sender and receiver must be synchronized; more complex but higher transmission rate.
points.partial_credit: Half if only one of these is given (e.g. frames/continuous block, or synchronization, or higher rate) without the grouping into frames.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both modes described with the contrast: async = per-character with start and stop bits (low rate); sync = frames/continuous stream of many characters, needing sender-receiver synchronization (higher rate). Give part marks when a mode is only half described or vague. A description of only one mode, or generic statements without start/stop bits or frames, earns about half at most.
